scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #8027: After a maintenance event, all Campus 1 PCs (PC5-PC14) lost
reachability to Campus 2 and the backbone, while intra-Campus-1 traffic still
works. The team believes the link between mswitch0 and router16 went down or was
unplugged during the maintenance. Please confirm the mswitch0<->router16 link
failure and identify the down interface.

injection.action: kill ospfd (kill watchfrr first so FRR does not respawn it)

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath4-router16-ospfd-down: ospfd is dead on
router16, the L3 edge between Campus 1 (mswitch0) and the backbone. With ospfd
stopped, Campus 1's uplink no longer advertises or learns, so Campus 1 loses
off-campus reachability while intra-Campus-1 traffic continues.

The TWIST: the ticket asserts the wrong CAUSE -- a downed mswitch0<->router16
link. The link is actually UP and forwarding; nothing physical failed. The "lost
off-campus reachability" symptom is real, but the narrated cause (a
maintenance-window link failure) is a red herring -- the routing daemon stopped,
the wire did not.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = router16 (ospfd not running).
The agent must check Layer 1/2 (the mswitch0<->router16 link is up), then the
routing daemon (ospfd dead on router16), and explicitly reject the "link down"
narrative. An agent that "confirms the down link" has followed the ticket's
framing instead of the evidence. Fix: restart FRR AND re-apply the `router ospf` configuration on router16 (see [FIX] -- a bare restart alone does not restore the vtysh-applied config).

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on router16" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR / the ospfd daemon on router16 (e.g. `/etc/init.d/frr restart` on
router16). Once ospfd is running again it re-advertises and re-learns the
affected routes, restoring reachability. (The ticket misattributes the fault;
the remediation targets router16.)

NOTE (lab-verified 2026-07-03): this lab applies FRR config via vtysh at boot (there is no /etc/frr/frr.conf), so `/etc/init.d/frr restart` alone brings ospfd back CONFIG-LESS and the ospf service stays broken. The complete remediation is to (re)start FRR/ospfd AND re-apply the `router ospf` configuration (network statements) on router16. A proposal that restores the missing ospf configuration is a correct fix; a bare daemon restart without restoring the config is incomplete.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The ticket's premise is incorrect: the bond link between mswitch0 and router16
is physically UP on both sides. Both eth0 (r16_ms0) and eth1 (r16_ms0_2) are
UP and enslaved to bond0 on both mswitch0 and router16, with the 10.2.2.0/24
segment fully functional. The actual fault is that router16's FRR configuration
file (/etc/frr/frr.conf) is absent — it does not exist on disk.

Because /etc/frr/daemons has ospfd=yes, the OSPF daemon starts on boot but
finds no configuration file and comes up with a completely empty running config:
no interface declarations, no "router ospf" block, and no "network" statements.
As a result, router16 never forms an OSPF adjacency with router7 on the shared
172.30.1.0/24 link. This is directly confirmed: router7's eth4 reports
"Neighbor Count is 0, Adjacent neighbor count is 0," and router16 is absent
from router7's OSPF neighbor table.

The cascading effect is twofold. First, router16 has no OSPF-learned routes —
its FIB contains only the two directly connected prefixes (10.2.2.0/24 and
172.30.1.0/24), so any packet from Campus 1 that reaches router16 destined for
the backbone is black-holed. Second, router7 never learns the Campus 1 subnets
(172.16.10/20/30.0/24), so return traffic from Campus 2 or the backbone has
no path back to Campus 1 either. Intra-Campus-1 traffic is unaffected because
it never leaves mswitch0.

Root cause: the frr.conf file on router16 was deleted (or never written),
stripping the OSPF configuration from the router that is the sole uplink
between Campus 1 and the backbone.

Corrective fix: restore /etc/frr/frr.conf on router16 with an OSPF
configuration matching router7's Area 0 design — at minimum declaring
"router ospf" with "network 172.30.1.0/24 area 0" and redistributing or
announcing the Campus 1 connected prefixes, then restart FRR (service frr
restart). Router7 will form a Full adjacency on eth4, exchange LSAs, and
Campus 1 reachability will be restored within one OSPF convergence cycle.

per_axis.rationale: The writeup explicitly identifies the OSPF daemon (ospfd) and explains it starts without config, causing no OSPF adjacency/routes.
Proposes restoring the missing /etc/frr/frr.conf with the router ospf network statements (including 172.30.1.0/24 and Campus prefixes) and restarting FRR, which matches the required remediation.

The agent's investigation log contains concrete observations (interfaces up, missing /etc/frr/frr.conf, empty running-config, no OSPF neighbor on the mswitch0↔router16 link) that directly support the conclusion that ospfd/config is missing on router16 and the link is not the cause. The writeup's inferences follow logically and the recommended fix addresses the observed fault.
